subject: Hosted API residency & retention impact assessment — MeridianHealth
messages:
From: Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@meridianhealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Chen <tom.chen@meridianhealth.com>, Legal Ops <legal.ops@meridianhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Oct 2026 14:10:00 -0400
Subject: Data residency & retention questionnaire — hosted API

Vivek,

Thanks for taking this — Meridian's procurement and security teams ran through Redwood's hosted API and we have a short set of clarifying questions to close our intake: 

1) Where are request/response payloads stored for hosted API customers by default (region-level)?
2) What are the default retention windows for request bodies, generated outputs, and any derived telemetry (SLO/metrics/traces)?
3) Do you maintain backups or snapshots containing customer data? If so, retention and regional placement?
4) How quickly can you delete a customer's data on request (soft delete vs permanent wipe)? Is there a programmatic API for this?
5) Which subprocessors/subcontractors might have access to persisted customer data for hosted deployments?
6) Can you provide an attestation or short evidence pack for our Security team (PDF + any CSV mapping region->storage)?

We attached our questionnaire (Meridian_RFI_v3.xlsx) — the answers can be high-level for now but we need timelines and an evidence artifact by 2026-11-03 to meet our compliance window.

Best,
Alicia Grant
Sr. Security Program Manager
MeridianHealth

[Attachment: Meridian_RFI_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency & retention questionnaire — hosted API

Hi Alicia — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Neha (technical infra) and Marissa (compliance) to provide the specifics and a small evidence pack. Quick summary up front so your team has context:

- Hosted API default storage region maps to the customer's selected region (we run multiregional control plane + region-scoped data stores).
- Default request/response bodies are retained for 30 days for debugging and quality monitoring; telemetry/metrics retained 90 days; audit logs retained 365 days.
- Backups (for DR) are encrypted, replicated across the same region class and retained 90 days by default.
- We support a Data Deletion API and customer-specific erasures are initiated within 48 hours and completed (surface deletion) within 7 days; deeper storage/backup purge timelines up to 90 days depending on the backup retention window.

Neha and Marissa — can you confirm the above and attach the CSV region map + retention playbook? Also we'll produce a one-page attestation PDF for Meridian's Security team by 2026-11-02. 

Thanks — Vivek
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@meridianhealth.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data residency & retention questionnaire — hosted API

Alicia — detailed answers below (pulled from Hosted API runbook & retention playbook). Attaching retention_playbook_v2.pdf and residency_map.csv for mapping of region -> S3 buckets / KMS region.

1) Region placement for request/response: Hosted API data at rest (customer request/response payloads and optional convo state) is stored in the customer-selected region (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, etc.). Control plane metadata is globally accessible but never contains raw request/response payloads. residency_map.csv (attached) lists current storage endpoints and KMS key regions.

2) Default retention windows:
- Request/response payloads: 30 days (default). We consider payloads "ephemeral persisted" — used for debugging, rate-limiting, and model quality audits. Customers may opt into extended retention (configurable to 1 year) with contract addendum.
- Generated outputs: treated the same as request/response; 30 days default.
- Telemetry/metrics/traces: 90 days (aggregated and sampled; full traces retained up to 30 days).
- Audit logs (authentication, config changes, deletion events): 365 days.

3) Backups/snapshots:
- Backups are encrypted with customer-region KMS keys (or our managed keys if the customer does not provide one).
- Backup retention default: 90 days. Backups are region-scoped and are not replicated outside the chosen region class unless the customer selects cross-region DR.

4) Deletion timelines & APIs:
- Soft-delete: immediate after request — metadata and pointers are marked deleted within 48 hours.
- Surface deletion: primary stores purged within 7 calendar days after the deletion job runs.
- Backup purge: backups are on a 90-day retention schedule; we run targeted backup purge jobs within 30 days of receipt of a legal/erasure request when required, but full irrevocable removal from offline backups can take up to 90 days depending on retention and snapshot chaining.
- Programmatic support: Data Deletion API (POST /v1/customers/{id}/erase) returns a job id. Job status is available via GET /v1/erase-jobs/{job_id}. We include an audit record with deletion timestamps.

5) Subprocessors:
- Cloud provider (regional object storage) and CDN providers for telemetry aggregation (names available on request).
- Monitoring & logging vendor for aggregated metrics (no raw payload access).
- We provide a subprocessors matrix PDF on request. No third-party has model parameter access; only region-scoped encrypted storage is used.

6) Evidence & attestation:
- Attached: retention_playbook_v2.pdf (procedures, timelines, sample job ids) and residency_map.csv (storage endpoints + KMS regions).
- We can provide a short signed attestation PDF and a sample deletion job trace for your legal team.

Technical notes / edge cases:
- Ephemeral caches: KV caches used during inference are in-memory and not persisted to long-term storage.
- Customer-managed KMS: recommended for regulated customers — when enabled, Redwood cannot decrypt backups without customer key rotation consent.

If you want, we can schedule a 30-minute technical walkthrough and provide a sample deletion job id you can watch as it runs.

— Neha Kapoor
Senior Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: retention_playbook_v2.pdf, residency_map.csv]

From: Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@meridianhealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Chen <tom.chen@meridianhealth.com>, Legal Ops <legal.ops@meridianhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Data residency & retention questionnaire — hosted API

Neha — this is very helpful, thanks. A couple of follow-ups for Security: 
- Can the Data Deletion API response include the storage objects that were purged (object ids) so our team can reconcile?
- For backups, if we enable customer-managed keys, can we get an SLA-backed guarantee that backups will not leave the selected region class?

Also, Legal Ops asked if you can supply a one-page signed attestation that lists the default retention windows and the expected longest purge time (i.e., 90 days due to backups). We'll need that by EOD 2026-11-03. Can you confirm?

Best,
Alicia

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Grant <alicia.grant@meridianhealth.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Data residency & retention questionnaire — hosted API

Alicia — confirmed. Short answers: 

- Data Deletion API: yes — the job response can include the listing of object identifiers and a signed audit record for reconciliation. We'll redact any internal IDs that are not meaningful to customers, but object ids/paths and timestamps will be sharable.
- Backups + CMK: when customer-managed KMS is enabled, backups are encrypted with the customer's key and stored in the chosen region class; cross-region replication only happens with explicit customer opt-in. We'll include an SLA note in the attestation.

Attached: Meridian_Retention_Attestation.pdf (one-page attestation signed by Redwood Compliance). Please confirm receipt and we'll mark the procurement checklist complete on our side. Happy to jump on a call if Legal wants a short walkthrough.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Meridian_Retention_Attestation.pdf]
